node.statement: ∀ {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (p r : ℝ), 0 < p → p < 1 → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → ExpandingCodes.SharpThreshold.TwoPointContraction p r → ∀ f : Finset I → ℝ, ExpandingCodes.Erasure.expectation p (fun E => ExpandingCodes.SharpThreshold.noise p r f E ^ 2) ≤ (ExpandingCodes.Erasure.expectation p (fun E => |f E| ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ))) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)
node.proof_route: Expand finite Fourier noise into a product kernel; tensorize the supplied scalar contraction by finite-coordinate induction and weighted Minkowski.

steps: Finset.prod_one_add expands the finite product kernel into the r-weighted character sum.
Swap the two finite sums in the explicit Fourier definition to identify noise with productNoiseOn univ, without Parseval or inversion.
Apply Real.Lp_add_le_of_nonneg at exponent 3/2 after absorbing each atom weight raised to 2/3 into the inputs.
Raise the weighted Minkowski inequality to 3/2, obtaining the finite mixed-norm interchange.
Condition expectationOn (insert i s) on whether i is present. Other coordinates are unchanged by insertion, giving an explicit two-branch kernel recurrence.
Compute the four one-coordinate kernel values using sqrt(p*(1-p))^2=p*(1-p), then apply the given TwoPointContraction.

Induct on the finite coordinate set s. The scalar contraction bounds the output pair pointwise; mixed-norm interchange moves the remaining expectations outside the pair; the two induction hypotheses complete the step.
Specialize the proved productNoiseOn_contract theorem to univ and rewrite back to the frozen noise definition.
proof_route.integrity: No analytic hypotheses were added, no final hypercontractivity or sharp-threshold statement is assumed, no Parseval dependency is needed. The exact frozen theorem signature, including the bounds on r, is preserved. The helper induction actually does not require those r bounds because the supplied scalar contraction already suffices.
